abstract: Streaming digital humans produce detailed video while continuing speech as new text arrives. High-resolution denoising is costly, and text updates can cause repeated or interrupted speech. We present TaoMate-HD, an autoregressive model for high-resolution audio-video streaming. For each short segment, or chunk, two denoising steps establish coarse video structure at low resolution. A final step refines the video to high resolution, with audio generated throughout the same trajectory. Each stage passes its audiovisual predictions to the same stage of the next chunk as history. Across text updates, the model retains this history to infer what has already been spoken. Continuation training utilizes asymmetric text conditioning, with separate text windows for generation and distillation. Experiments show a $1.6\times$ speedup over direct high-resolution generation with the same model and hardware. Optimized stage-parallel deployment provides a further $1.9\times$ overall speedup over serial progressive generation. Our continuation training reduces character error rate by 11.18 percentage points relative to the baseline. The model also supports hour-long audiovisual generation. Our project page is https://taoliveaigc.github.io/TaoMate-HD.

sections.body: The paper states that high-resolution synthesis is expensive and that text updates can disrupt ongoing speech. It contrasts direct high-resolution generation, few-step distillation, progressive-resolution methods, and stage-parallel inference. It notes that faster processing of one chunk still waits for final refinement before the next chunk can use it as history. The proposed model runs two low-resolution denoising steps and one high-resolution step per chunk, and it keeps audiovisual history across text-window changes. Its stated aim is to reuse predictions before final refinement completes.
sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.headline: TaoMate-HD targets high-resolution audiovisual streaming, where dense denoising is costly and text updates can repeat or interrupt speech.

sections.body: The related work groups prior methods into few-step autoregressive audio-video generation, progressive spatial computation, and temporal memory with denoising parallelism. It notes that CausVid and Self Forcing train on student-generated histories, and that PyramidalWan adapts a teacher to multiple resolutions. It states that stage-parallel inference keeps stage-specific history at the stage's output noise level. The paper says it instead uses paired clean audiovisual predictions on each stage's native grid as a shared history representation.
sections.heading: 2 Related Work
sections.headline: Related work covers few-step distillation, progressive resolution, and stage-parallel inference, which uses history at stage output noise levels.

sections.body:
- Each chunk runs two evaluations on a 480×864 grid, then one on a 768×1376 grid, with audio on the same latent geometry throughout.
- Each stage's clean estimate is encoded at zero noise on its native grid and stored in that stage's history bank for the next chunk.
- High-grid and low-grid noise are coupled so the high-resolution step receives standard Gaussian noise.
- Continuation training uses the model's own rollouts, with separate text windows for the generator and the distillation scores.
sections.heading: 3 Method
sections.headline: Chunks denoise in two low-resolution steps and one high-resolution step, with each stage's clean prediction reused as history.

sections.body: Table 1 compares TaoMate-HD with audio-video, speech-to-video, and streaming systems on VABench metrics, Whisper-based character error rate, and throughput. Serial TaoMate-HD reports 19.57% character error and 4.68 FPS, and the parallel configuration reports 8.99 FPS in Table 2. Progressive generation gives a $1.60\times$ spatial speedup and deployment gives a $1.92\times$ overall speedup. Table 3 shows that asymmetric distillation lowers character error from 30.751% to 19.570%. Timing uses eight H20 GPUs, and quality is measured on 100 self-constructed sequences.
sections.heading: 4 Experiments
sections.headline: Serial TaoMate-HD scores highest on Temporal and AudioAes among streaming generators, reaching 0.913 and 4.407.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the $1.60\times$ progressive speedup, the further $1.92\times$ deployment speedup, and the reduction of character error from 30.8% to 19.6%. It attributes speech continuity to retained audiovisual history and asymmetric distillation. It states that these advances support generation extending to an hour. The hour-long support rests on demonstrations; the sections provided report no quantitative hour-long metric, and the quantitative evaluation covers self-constructed sequences only.
sections.heading: 5 Conclusion
sections.headline: The conclusion summarizes gains from progressive denoising and asymmetric distillation, extending to an hour of streaming.
